name: Pareto front for competing objectives
when: 两个以上目标互相冲突，不能同时最优，需要给出取舍集合而不是单一解
when_not: 目标可以加权成单一指标且权重有客观依据 → 直接用加权和；目标其实不冲突 → 前沿无信息量
assumptions: All objectives have been oriented the same way, all minimised or all maximised. Otherwise dominance is undefined.
The sampled designs cover the body of the design space, so the front is observed rather than extrapolated.
The conflict between objectives is real, not an artefact of too few samples.
breaks_when: Fewer than about 50 samples: the front holds only a handful of points, and its shape between them is interpolation rather than evidence.
The objectives are strongly correlated: the front degenerates to a line, which means the two objectives are measuring one thing.
A feasibility boundary is active: infeasible designs must not appear on the front, and a front computed without the constraint is meaningless.
report_must_include: number of front points against the total
the definition of the feasible set
refs: Pareto, V. (1906). Manuale di Economia Politica. Milan: Societa Editrice Libraria.
Deb, K. (2001). Multi-Objective Optimization Using Evolutionary Algorithms. Chichester: Wiley.
